findings.reason: a `done` declaration retires a deliverable the plan still owes, so no node will ever refresh the eleven-row gate and its ordering constraint is invisible to admission.
findings.text: §3 is declared `done` in `plan-section-declarations` and carries no `depends-on`, yet its own landed summary says "One measurement remains owed rather than designed: the eleven-row receipt is refreshed after `millisecond-converged-solve` §2 makes the prescribed current a traced argument", and that section is still `implementable`; the dependency map has no `s3` key and `plan-informs` does not name the plan this section waits on

findings.reason: §6 and §13 have already landed, so nothing queues differently, but the declaration is not a faithful record of what the section consumes.
findings.text: §9's declared `depends-on` is `[s7, s8],` while its own prose requires the re-solve to run "at the head carrying §6, §7 and §8" (§6 is the booked finite-edge source the rows are solved on) and it reports convergence on §13's finite-edge profiles

findings.reason: a node running the control through the probe route it is shown in clause (1) reproduces 1119994.165 and records a failed control on faithful code, while a node choosing the benchmark route passes; the target is only measurable once the route and the 160.6 A discrepancy are settled.
findings.text: clause (2) requires the zero-edge-cap control to reproduce "the pre-§13 reading of 1119833.584 A within 2e-6" while clause (1) sets the record beside "the probe's 1119994.165 A", and both are readings of the same pre-§13 frame: they differ by 160.6 A (1.43e-4), 71 times the stated tolerance, and the section records the probe route and the benchmark route as sharing "conductor count and adapter path" without explaining the gap or saying which route the control must use

findings.reason: unlike §7, §11 and §13, §9 leaves a writing node to choose its record path, and the natural reading points at a peer record the section itself forbids replacing ("never in their place"); naming the new fragment removes both the overwrite risk and a done-when no later reader can open by path.
findings.text: §9 names no durable path for the refitted vector's receipt or for the record that tabulates both arms; it says only "commit it as a receipt beside the evidence fragment", and clause (3)'s "The evidence fragment tabulates both arms per row" resolves to the existing `docs/evidence/fragments/diiid-vertical-force-balance/diiid-xpoint-coil-correction.html`, which already carries the earlier measured-current arm

findings.reason: the triage directory exists but holds no such file, so the pointer is dead; the three facts it is cited for (seed correct, total current correct, external field the leading suspect and later closed negative) are restated in full in the same paragraph and in §2, so nothing a node needs is lost.

the repository's commit rules forbid plan, sprint and section identifiers in commit messages, so a node that follows the clause exactly breaks a binding rule; the mechanism ("the finite-edge flux-function form") can be named instead of the section number.
findings.text: §11 clause (3) requires the node to re-register "naming the three accepted changes and §13 in the commit body", putting a plan-section identifier into a commit message

findings.reason: these name committed measurement instruments the receipt must be reproducible from, not code a node is told to write or extend; dropping them would make the numbers unreproducible, so the plan's authority is better served keeping them while the router-override note stays in the brief.
findings.text: §9 prescribes "running the committed fit (`scripts/prototypes/diiid_xpoint_coil_correction/fit.py`) at the head" and a receipt format, and §11:108 fixes the "benchmark's own entry point with `--output`" route, which are a code path, a step sequence and a flag rather than only the record and its tolerance

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the header's triage pointer names a file that no longer exists; every other cited file, fragment, figure directory, plan and receipt that the plan relies on resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11's negative control targets a pre-§13 value that its own evidence records twice, 160.6 A apart, under a 2e-6 tolerance.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §9 names no durable path for its fitted-arms receipt or record.
rubric_items.naming: a finding — §11 instructs the node to write a plan-section label into a commit body.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9 and §11 name the committed instrument and command-line route rather than only the record; the three substantive checks (root cause against cited evidence, reachability of the endpoint, no formula or function to implement) otherwise hold for every section.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each open section (§7, §9, §11) names one deliverable: the compensator mask measured on all four rows, the corrected-current arms, and the pinned-frame re-registration.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §3 is declared `done` while its own text owes an eleven-row gate that waits on a section of another plan, and no dependency records that wait.
